cvs: 'Midnight Rose Select' – denser pink speckling · 'Palace Purple' – plain bronze-purple, larger · 'Obsidian' – glossy near-black, no speckles · 'Plum Pudding' – plum with silver sheen
foliage: evergreen; rounded lobed leaves, deep purple-black with pink speckles
hardinessNote: Hardy in all of the UK including very cold winters, approximately -20 to -15°C.
prune: Remove tatty or scorched leaves in spring and cut spent flower stems. Lift and divide every 3–4 years when crowns turn woody.
resilience: Tough evergreen mound; leaf colour is best in light shade. Crowns lift and go woody with age. Pests: vine weevil grubs (especially in pots), occasional rust.
soilWarning: Waterlogged winter soil rots the crown
uncertain: peak: sold on foliage, Apr-Oct is the leaf season; small cream flowers in late spring
height/spread: RHS 0.1–0.5 m; nurseries 25–45 × 38–45 cm, draft figures kept
ratings from draft and the deck's Heuchera siblings
uses: Front of border · containers · woodland edge · ground cover · foliage contrast
visual: Near-black purple leaves splashed hot pink, fading to cream in autumn · evergreen mound
water: Water regularly in the first summer and in dry spells; keep pots evenly moist but never sitting wet.
